fairness_rules: No cross-theory numerical performance claim without identical equations and conventions.
Source-published values are not Symtropy-reproduced values.
A low collocation residual is not a full-domain enclosure.
A full-domain residual enclosure is not by itself an existence theorem.
A local existence theorem does not establish EFT validity or observational admissibility.
Inconclusive is not refuted and not verified.
Akribeia's 5D/7D Lovelock cases are not directly comparable to 4D pure-Weyl cases; compare only after action/dimension/ansatz/gauge/boundary matching.
Akribeia's reported ~1e-160 relative L2 error is a Myers-Perry GR-limit result at 300-digit precision, not a universal error on all higher-curvature branches.
Akribeia's continuous neural-field certification and quantified residuals are not to be equated automatically with an interval/radii-polynomial existence theorem.
The two static reduced Bach equations are distinct: the factorized B1+B2 equation selects the four-term profile; B1-B2 then imposes Q=0. Both must be checked.
The Akribeia 10^-160 relative L2 figure is specific to the five-dimensional Myers-Perry GR-limit control at 300 digits; it is not an EGB equation-residual bound.
The Akribeia 5D EGB equal-spin case must not be compared directly to the current 4D static pure-Weyl code. A dimension/action/symmetry/gauge/boundary matched adapter is required.
The current public symtropy-relativity metric component representation is 4x4; 5D work requires an explicit dimension-generalized or invariant-frame formulation.
The 5D equal-spin MP control is expressed in the g=r^2 radial gauge; do not confuse r_H in this gauge with the Boyer-Lindquist radial horizon coordinate.
The MP exact b,f,h,w profiles must all be checked; b,w alone are not a complete metric control.

The EGB rotational Noether flux from the 2010 reduced action is a separate exact conserved quantity; quadrature reconstruction of w requires an interval proof that its radial denominator K(r) stays away from zero.
The 2010 action and gauge-fixed ansatz are used as an independent source for the Akribeia benchmark; no raw nonzero-alpha EGB profiles have yet been reproduced.
The full time-sector Eq. (2.14) radial current includes alpha-dependent terms; the Einstein-only current r^2(h*w*w'-b') is incomplete at finite alpha.
The time-sector current is sourced: P_t'=(alpha/6)*r^2*sqrt(b*h/f)*L_GB. Its asymptotic endpoint is 2U, but it is not a conserved charge at finite alpha.
Only the angular P_w current is the conserved Noether current in this two-current discussion. Do not construct a dual-conserved-flux reduction.
A source-balanced b-prime reconstruction must use the full alpha-dependent coefficient and the local P_t(r), not the asymptotic constant 2U at every radius.
The 5D radial-action oracle must be varied before g=r² is substituted; retain E_g after gauge slicing and check all five residuals on exact MP and BD branches.
The fourth Einstein-Hilbert radial-action term is b*g'*h'/h; exact branch controls reject b*g'*h'/g.
Include the published finite-alpha 5D slow-rotation control as an intermediate validation rung between static BD and fully nonlinear rotating EGB.

For the slow-rotation background F=BD, the angular flux denominator K=r²-alpha(F-1)=r²*s is analytically positive and satisfies K>=r² for alpha>=0; this does not prove K stays nonzero for arbitrary nonlinear candidates.

The 2010 classical comparator is a Newton-Raphson BVP solver with adaptive mesh, typically 100-1000 points and reported typical relative accuracy ~1e-6; compare common observables and recomputed residual norms rather than equating this with Akribeia's residual metric.
The matched solver matrix must include the classical 2010 BVP solver, Akribeia neural-to-Chebyshev refinement, and Symtropy's action/Noether/perturbative continuation pipeline.
Symtropy is not considered superior until it reproduces 2010 observables and demonstrates a matched work-precision advantage plus independent residual/domain qualification.
Lam-Chung-Yunes 2026 arbitrary-spin spectral metrics are a methodological high-spin comparator only: their 4D leading-coupling EFT equations differ from the 5D pure EGB target.
Map the accuracy-vs-spin envelope for each perturbative order and observable; do not claim a universal slow-rotation breakdown spin.
Reproduce the 2010 two-gauge cross-check by comparing invariant physical observables and transformed field residuals.
The derived O(a^2) even-sector E_b,E_f,E_g,E_h system must recover exact Myers-Perry B2,F2,H2 at alpha=0; retain E_g as radial constraint.
Do not claim finite-alpha spin-squared backreaction until the inhomogeneous BVP is solved with independent horizon, infinity, spectral and first-law checks.
